svg.title: The nurse is matching each infant's exam findings to the most likely congenital heart defect.
svg.desc: Coarctation of the aorta narrows the aorta so pressure and pulses fall distal to the narrowing, producing the classic arm-leg blood pressure gradient and weak femoral pulses. A patent ductus arteriosus keeps a fetal vessel open between the aorta and pulmonary artery, producing a continuous machinery murmur with bounding pulses from the wide pulse pressure. Tetralogy of Fallot shunts deoxygenated blood into the systemic circulation, causing progressive cyanosis and hypercyanotic 'Tet' spells, while an ASD's fixed split S2 with few symptoms reflects a low-pressure shunt between the atria. Transposition of the great arteries runs systemic and pulmonary circulations in parallel rather than in series, causing severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen; VSD and tricuspid atresia present differently and do not match any description here.
